svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Point mutations change one base in a gene. Here: the mRNA codons and the amino acids they code for."], [1.5, "Silent: CUU \u2192 CUC still codes for leucine."], [4, "Missense: GAG \u2192 GUG codes for valine instead of glutamic acid (the sickle-cell mutation)."], [6.5, "Nonsense: UGG \u2192 UGA is a stop codon, so translation ends early."], [9, "Insertion: one extra base shifts the reading frame."], [11.5, "Deletion: one missing base also shifts the reading frame."]]
svg.title: Point mutations
svg.desc: An mRNA sequence and its amino acids compared with silent, missense and nonsense substitutions and frameshift insertion and deletion, with the changed base highlighted.
svg.text: mRNA codons (read 5′ → 3′). Red outline: the changed base. Orange: codons shifted by a frameshift.

g.data-info: Three bases of mRNA that code for one amino acid (or stop).
One base is replaced by another. Because the code is degenerate, the effect may be silent, missense or nonsense.

g.text: same amino acid: no change to

g.data-info: Inserting or deleting one base shifts the reading frame: every codon after it changes, usually giving a non-functional protein.
